source.original_text: Let n>=3, kappa>=4 and ell>=0. On full real O(n), use the existing normalized Borel Haar probability mu; on Euclidean real n-space use its actual norm and volume. Let A_O be the literal Eq4 precision and p_O(x)=sqrt(det A_O)/(2pi)^(n/2) exp(-x^T A_O x/2), with real n/2. Put U=O_11 and a(O)=kappa+1+4ell-(kappa-1)U. Both joint functions f(O,x)=det(O)exp(-ell||x||_2^2)p_O(x) and g(O,x)=det(O)sqrt(det A_O)/(2pi)^(n/2) exp(-a(O)||x||_2^2/4) are absolutely Bochner L1 under mu times Euclidean volume. Moreover the literal nested transform E[det(O) integral exp(-ell||x||_2^2)p_O(x) dx] equals (-1)^(n-1)(sqrt(kappa)-1)^(n-1)/2^(n/2) times E[((sqrt(kappa)+1)U-(sqrt(kappa)-1))/a(O)^(n/2)]. This includes ell=0. It is an equality for explicit real formulas, without identifying p with an actual Gaussian density or the transform with target-mixture expectations.

∀ {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) {κ : ℝ}
    (hκ : 4 ≤ κ) {ℓ : ℝ} (hℓ : 0 ≤ ℓ),
    let j0 : Fin n := ⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩
    let U : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → ℝ :=
      fun O => (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) j0 j0
    let a : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → ℝ :=
      fun O => κ + 1 + 4 * ℓ - (κ - 1) * U O
    let p : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ :=
      fun O x => Real.sqrt ((((κ + 1) / 2) • (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) - ((κ - 1) / 4) • ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) + (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose))).det /
        (2 * Real.pi) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) *
          Real.exp (-((WithLp.ofLp x) ⬝ᵥ
            ((((κ + 1) / 2) • (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) - ((κ - 1) / 4) • ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) + (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose)) *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x)) / 2)
    let f : (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) → ℝ :=
      fun z => (z.1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det *
        (Real.exp (-ℓ * ‖z.2‖ ^ 2) * p z.1 z.2)
    let g : (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) → ℝ :=
      fun z => (z.1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det *
        Real.sqrt ((((κ + 1) / 2) • (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) - ((κ - 1) / 4) • ((z.1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) + (z.1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose))).det /
          (2 * Real.pi) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) * Real.exp (-a z.1 * ‖z.2‖ ^ 2 / 4)
    Integrable f (((Measure.haarMeasure (⊤ : PositiveCompacts (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ)))).prod volume) ∧
    Integrable g (((Measure.haarMeasure (⊤ : PositiveCompacts (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ)))).prod volume) ∧
    (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
      (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det *
        (∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), Real.exp (-ℓ * ‖x‖ ^ 2) * p O x)
        ∂(Measure.haarMeasure (⊤ : PositiveCompacts (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ)))) =
      ((-1 : ℝ) ^ (n - 1) * (Real.sqrt κ - 1) ^ (n - 1) /
        (2 : ℝ) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2)) *
        (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
          ((Real.sqrt κ + 1) * U O - (Real.sqrt κ - 1)) /
            (a O) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) ∂(Measure.haarMeasure (⊤ : PositiveCompacts (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ))))

import AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.KernelAxis
import AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.RadialIntegral
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.Prod
import Mathlib.Tactic.Positivity

/-!
# Genuine Fubini for the literal signed Gaussian mixture transform

Zhou--Suzuki arXiv:2610.20492v1, Appendix B.2.2, H definition through Eq21.
Joint Haar-times-Euclidean-volume L1 is produced internally. A finite compact
prefactor is a sufficient alternative to the sharp source Ex59 prefactor.
Actual Gaussian density/law identification and mixture/TV meanings stay separate.
-/

open Matrix MeasureTheory Set TopologicalSpace
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.OrthogonalHaar
open AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.DeterminantFamily
open AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.KernelAxis
open AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.RadialIntegral

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.MixtureFubini

private lemma gaussian_decay_integrable {n : ℕ} :
    Integrable (fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) => Real.exp (-‖x‖ ^ 2 / 2)) volume := by
  have hc := GaussianFourier.integrable_cexp_neg_mul_sq_norm_add
    (V := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
    (b := ((1 / 2 : ℝ) : ℂ)) (by norm_num) 0 0
  convert hc.re using 1
  funext x
  simp only [zero_mul, add_zero]
  rw [← Complex.ofReal_pow, ← Complex.ofReal_neg, ← Complex.ofReal_mul,
    ← Complex.ofReal_exp]
  congr 1
  ring

private lemma joint_integrable {n : ℕ}
    (k : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → ℝ)
    (b : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ)
    (hk : Continuous k) (hb : Continuous b)
    (hbound : ∀ z, b z ≤ -‖z.2‖ ^ 2 / 2) :
    Integrable (fun z => k z.1 * Real.exp (b z)) ((orthogonalHaar n).prod volume) := by
  let := (orthogonalHaar_spec n).1
  obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := isCompact_univ.exists_bound_of_continuousOn hk.continuousOn
  have hmajor := (integrable_const C (μ := orthogonalHaar n)).mul_prod
    (gaussian_decay_integrable (n := n))
  apply hmajor.mono' ((hk.comp continuous_fst).mul (Real.continuous_exp.comp hb)).aestronglyMeasurable
  exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun z => by
    change ‖k z.1 * Real.exp (b z)‖ ≤ C * Real.exp (-‖z.2‖ ^ 2 / 2)
    rw [norm_mul, Real.norm_of_nonneg (Real.exp_pos (b z)).le]
    calc
      ‖k z.1‖ * Real.exp (b z) ≤ ‖k z.1‖ * Real.exp (-‖z.2‖ ^ 2 / 2) :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (Real.exp_le_exp.mpr (hbound z)) (norm_nonneg _)
      _ ≤ C * Real.exp (-‖z.2‖ ^ 2 / 2) :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hC z.1 (mem_univ _)) (Real.exp_pos _).le

theorem literal_mixture_transform {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) {κ : ℝ}
    (hκ : 4 ≤ κ) {ℓ : ℝ} (hℓ : 0 ≤ ℓ) :
    let j0 : Fin n := ⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩
    let U : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → ℝ :=
      fun O => (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) j0 j0
    let a : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → ℝ :=
      fun O => κ + 1 + 4 * ℓ - (κ - 1) * U O
    let p : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ :=
      fun O x => Real.sqrt (singleBlockPrecision κ O).det /
        (2 * Real.pi) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) *
          Real.exp (-((WithLp.ofLp x) ⬝ᵥ
            (singleBlockPrecision κ O *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x)) / 2)
    let f : (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) → ℝ :=
      fun z => (z.1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det *
        (Real.exp (-ℓ * ‖z.2‖ ^ 2) * p z.1 z.2)
    let g : (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) → ℝ :=
      fun z => (z.1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det *
        Real.sqrt (singleBlockPrecision κ z.1).det /
          (2 * Real.pi) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) * Real.exp (-a z.1 * ‖z.2‖ ^ 2 / 4)
    Integrable f ((orthogonalHaar n).prod volume) ∧
    Integrable g ((orthogonalHaar n).prod volume) ∧
    (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
      (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det *
        (∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), Real.exp (-ℓ * ‖x‖ ^ 2) * p O x)
        ∂orthogonalHaar n) =
      ((-1 : ℝ) ^ (n - 1) * (Real.sqrt κ - 1) ^ (n - 1) /
        (2 : ℝ) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2)) *
        (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
          ((Real.sqrt κ + 1) * U O - (Real.sqrt κ - 1)) /
            (a O) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) ∂orthogonalHaar n) := by
  classical
  let j0 : Fin n := ⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩
  let U : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → ℝ :=
    fun O => (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) j0 j0
  let a : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → ℝ :=
    fun O => κ + 1 + 4 * ℓ - (κ - 1) * U O
  let p : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ :=
    fun O x => Real.sqrt (singleBlockPrecision κ O).det /
      (2 * Real.pi) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) *
        Real.exp (-((WithLp.ofLp x) ⬝ᵥ
          (singleBlockPrecision κ O *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x)) / 2)
  let f : (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) → ℝ :=
    fun z => (z.1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det *
      (Real.exp (-ℓ * ‖z.2‖ ^ 2) * p z.1 z.2)
  let g : (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) → ℝ :=
    fun z => (z.1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det *
      Real.sqrt (singleBlockPrecision κ z.1).det /
        (2 * Real.pi) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) * Real.exp (-a z.1 * ‖z.2‖ ^ 2 / 4)
  let q (O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :=
    (WithLp.ofLp x) ⬝ᵥ (singleBlockPrecision κ O *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x)
  let k (O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) :=
    (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * Real.sqrt (singleBlockPrecision κ O).det /
      (2 * Real.pi) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2)
  let r (O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :=
    Real.sqrt (singleBlockPrecision κ O).det / (2 * Real.pi) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) *
      Real.exp (-(κ + 1 - (κ - 1) * U O) * ‖x‖ ^ 2 / 4)
  change Integrable f ((orthogonalHaar n).prod volume) ∧
    Integrable g ((orthogonalHaar n).prod volume) ∧ _
  let := (orthogonalHaar_spec n).1
  have hAc : Continuous (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ => singleBlockPrecision κ O) := by
    unfold singleBlockPrecision
    exact continuous_const.sub
      ((continuous_subtype_val.add continuous_subtype_val.matrix_transpose).const_smul ((κ - 1) / 4))
  have hk : Continuous k := by dsimp only [k]; fun_prop
  have hUc : Continuous U := continuous_subtype_val.matrix_elem j0 j0
  have hac : Continuous a := by dsimp only [a]; fun_prop
  have hqc : Continuous (fun z : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) =>
      q z.1 z.2) := by dsimp only [q]; fun_prop
  have hq (O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :
      ‖x‖ ^ 2 ≤ q O x := by
    have h := ((singleBlockPrecision_regular hn hκ O).2 (WithLp.ofLp x)).1
    have he : (WithLp.ofLp x) ⬝ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x = ‖x‖ ^ 2 := by
      rw [EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq]
      simp only [dotProduct, pow_two]
    simpa only [he] using h
  have ha (O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) : 2 ≤ a O := by
    have hu : U O ≤ 1 := le_trans (le_abs_self _) (by
      simpa only [U, Real.norm_eq_abs] using entry_norm_bound_of_unitary O.property j0 j0)
    have hm := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hu (show 0 ≤ κ - 1 by linarith)
    dsimp only [a]
    linarith
  have hf : Integrable f ((orthogonalHaar n).prod volume) := by
    have hi := joint_integrable k (fun z => -ℓ * ‖z.2‖ ^ 2 + -(q z.1 z.2) / 2) hk
      (by fun_prop) (fun z => by
        have h1 := hq z.1 z.2
        have h2 := mul_nonneg hℓ (sq_nonneg ‖z.2‖)
        linarith)
    convert hi using 1
    funext z
    dsimp only [f, p, k, q]
    rw [Real.exp_add]
    ring
  have hg : Integrable g ((orthogonalHaar n).prod volume) := by
    have hi := joint_integrable k (fun z => -a z.1 * ‖z.2‖ ^ 2 / 4) hk
      (by fun_prop) (fun z => by
        have hm := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (ha z.1) (sq_nonneg ‖z.2‖)
        nlinarith)
    exact hi
  refine ⟨hf, hg, ?_⟩
  have haxis (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :
      (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
        (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * p O x ∂orthogonalHaar n) =
      (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
        (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * r O x ∂orthogonalHaar n) :=
    (signed_kernel_radial hn hκ x).2.2
  have hgr (O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :
      g (O, x) = Real.exp (-ℓ * ‖x‖ ^ 2) *
        ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * r O x) := by
    dsimp only [g, r, a]
    rw [show Real.exp (-ℓ * ‖x‖ ^ 2) *
        ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det *
          (Real.sqrt (singleBlockPrecision κ O).det / (2 * Real.pi) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) *
            Real.exp (-(κ + 1 - (κ - 1) * U O) * ‖x‖ ^ 2 / 4))) =
      ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * Real.sqrt (singleBlockPrecision κ O).det /
        (2 * Real.pi) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2)) *
          (Real.exp (-ℓ * ‖x‖ ^ 2) * Real.exp (-(κ + 1 - (κ - 1) * U O) * ‖x‖ ^ 2 / 4)) by ring]
    rw [← Real.exp_add]
    congr 1
    congr 1
    ring
  have havg (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :
      (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ, f (O, x) ∂orthogonalHaar n) =
      (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ, g (O, x) ∂orthogonalHaar n) := by
    calc
      _ = Real.exp (-ℓ * ‖x‖ ^ 2) *
          (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
            (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * p O x ∂orthogonalHaar n) := by
        rw [← integral_const_mul]
        apply integral_congr_ae
        exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun O => by dsimp only [f]; ring
      _ = Real.exp (-ℓ * ‖x‖ ^ 2) *
          (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
            (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * r O x ∂orthogonalHaar n) := by rw [haxis]
      _ = _ := by
        rw [← integral_const_mul]
        apply integral_congr_ae
        exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun O => (hgr O x).symm
  have heval := (radialized_test_integral hn hκ hℓ).2.2.2
  calc
    _ = ∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
        (∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), f (O, x)) ∂orthogonalHaar n := by
      apply integral_congr_ae
      exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun O => (integral_const_mul _ _).symm
    _ = ∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n),
        (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ, f (O, x) ∂orthogonalHaar n) :=
      integral_integral_swap hf
    _ = ∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n),
        (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ, g (O, x) ∂orthogonalHaar n) := by
      apply integral_congr_ae
      exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall havg
    _ = ∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
        (∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), g (O, x)) ∂orthogonalHaar n :=
      (integral_integral_swap hg).symm
    _ = (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
        (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * Real.sqrt (singleBlockPrecision κ O).det *
          (∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), Real.exp (-a O * ‖x‖ ^ 2 / 4))
          ∂orthogonalHaar n) / (2 * Real.pi) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) := by
      simp only [g, integral_const_mul]
      rw [← integral_div]
      apply integral_congr_ae
      exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun O => by ring
    _ = _ := heval

steps.title: Dominate the original joint integrand
steps.text: The existing exact precision theorem gives x^T A_O x>=||x||_2^2. Since ell>=0, adding the test exponent only increases decay. The determinant-normalization prefactor is continuous on compact full O(n), so its absolute value has a finite bound C. Thus the original joint integrand is bounded in absolute value by C exp(-||x||_2^2/2). This C is sufficient and is not claimed to equal the sharp source Ex59 prefactor.
steps.lean: hq consumes the exact singleBlockPrecision_regular and identifies coordinate dotProduct with true Euclidean squared norm. hk and private joint_integrable produce the compact bound and actual product L1 using GaussianFourier integrability.

steps.title: Dominate the radial joint integrand too
steps.text: Orthogonality bounds U<=1, hence a(O)>=2+4ell>=2. The radial exponent is bounded by -||x||_2^2/2, with the identical prefactor. The same genuine integrable majorant works on Haar times volume, including ell=0. Continuity supplies joint measurability, while the canonical Haar specification supplies probability.
steps.lean: ha uses entry_norm_bound_of_unitary. The private product provider combines compact continuity with actual Haar probability and GaussianFourier decay; hf and hg are genuine joint Integrable proofs.

steps.title: Perform the first legitimate Fubini swap
steps.text: Pull the determinant into each spatial integral and apply Fubini using the proved original joint L1. The original nested transform becomes a spatial integral of signed Haar averages. steps.lean: The main calc uses integral_const_mul and integral_integral_swap hf. No spatial integrability hypothesis is supplied by the caller.

steps.text: For each fixed Euclidean x, the already compiled norm-axis theorem equates the signed original average with its exact O11 radial formula. The test exp(-ell||x||_2^2) is constant in O. Multiplying that equality by the test and combining exponents identifies the two Haar inner integrals. steps.title: Use radial joint L1 for the second swap
steps.text: Apply Fubini in the reverse direction to the radial joint integrand. Pull the unchanged normalizer and determinant factors outside the spatial integral. This yields precisely the iterated expression already evaluated in the existing radial-integral theorem.
steps.lean: The calc uses (integral_integral_swap hg).symm, integral_const_mul and integral_div. Both swaps have their own proved joint L1 provider, on the same actual measures.

reconstruction.text:
For every natural number n with 3 <= n, every real kappa with 4 <= kappa, and every real ell with 0 <= ell (including ell = 0), make the following literal definitions. Let G = O(n, R) be the full real orthogonal matrix group, containing both determinant signs, and let E = EuclideanSpace R (Fin n), identified through WithLp.ofLp with R^n. Let mu be Measure.haarMeasure(top : PositiveCompacts G), the actual normalized Haar probability measure on G, and let vol be the canonical Euclidean volume measure on E. Use the true Euclidean norm on E. Let j0 be the coordinate 0 in Fin n, let U(O) = O[j0,j0], and define
A(O) = ((kappa + 1)/2) I_n - ((kappa - 1)/4) (O + O^T),
a(O) = kappa + 1 + 4 ell - (kappa - 1) U(O),
p(O,x) = sqrt(det A(O)) / (2 pi)^(n/2) * exp(-(x dot (A(O) x))/2),
f(O,x) = det(O) * (exp(-ell ||x||_2^2) * p(O,x)),
g(O,x) = det(O) * sqrt(det A(O)) / (2 pi)^(n/2) * exp(-a(O) ||x||_2^2/4).
Here x dot (A(O) x) is the real coordinate dot product supplied by WithLp.ofLp. Every displayed square root is Real.sqrt, the nonnegative real square root. Each dimension-half exponent n/2 is the real number (n : R)/2 and its power is a real power; each exponent n-1 is natural subtraction in N and its power is a natural power.
The conclusion is the conjunction of these three outputs:
(1) f is absolutely Bochner integrable with respect to the product measure mu x vol on G x E;
(2) g is absolutely Bochner integrable with respect to the same product measure;
(3) the following real Bochner integral equality holds:
integral_G det(O) * (integral_E exp(-ell ||x||_2^2) * p(O,x) dvol(x)) dmu(O)
= [(-1)^(n-1) * (sqrt(kappa) - 1)^(n-1) / 2^(n/2)]
  * integral_G [((sqrt(kappa) + 1) * U(O) - (sqrt(kappa) - 1)) / a(O)^(n/2)] dmu(O).
All functions above are the literal real formulas displayed; p is not replaced by an independently characterized Gaussian law. The two joint integrability assertions are conclusions, not hypotheses, and no caller-supplied majorant or Fubini hypothesis is assumed. Integrals use the Mathlib Bochner integration convention.
